extra.message: User-controlled searchText is concatenated directly into the SQL string passed to db.all() ("...where name like '%" + searchText + "%'"). This is reachable from POST /search (routes/search.js:11-13) and GET /api/search?searchText= (routes/api.js:7-10) and allows full SQL injection (e.g. UNION SELECT to exfiltrate the user table).

The Pug template uses unescaped interpolation '!=' to render 'Search Results for: ' + searchText. searchText comes directly from the request (routes/search.js:11) and is not sanitized, so a payload such as <script>alert(document.cookie)</script> is reflected and executed in the victim's browser.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Hardcoded administrative credentials are embedded in source code: userTbl.run('admin', 'S3cr37P@$$w0rD!'). The admin password is committed to the repository and seeded into the user table, exposing privileged credentials to anyone with source access.
On a database error the raw error object is returned to the client via res.json(err). This leaks internal database/stack details (including the failing SQL statement) to remote users.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The error template renders error.stack. app.js:42 only hides the error when app.get('env') is not 'development', but NODE_ENV is never set (see Dockerfile), so Express defaults to 'development' and full stack traces are returned to clients.
